M_fixed: Let P be a set of n points in Z^2 with coordinates in [-n^c,n^c] (c a large constant; small grids are trivial since a k x k grid holds at most 2k points with no three collinear), or in R^2 on the real RAM. Is there eps>0 and an algorithm deciding in O(n^{2-eps}) time whether three points of P are collinear? Alternatively: prove no O(n^{2-eps}) algorithm exists under a hypothesis not refuted by AVW (e.g. k-AP Hypothesis, 4SUM, OV).
notes: Posed by AVW (arXiv:2610.06783, Sec. 1 and Sec. 6): 'now open whether ... three collinear points ... truly subquadratic'. Verified AVW/Majdoddin claims (real 3SUM Las Vegas, since derandomized by Chan-Itakura-Ma-Yu 2610.42012). Fischer 2610.32162 recovers many GeomBase lower bounds under k-AP but explicitly not 3-points-on-a-line. Original M was not a statement; fixed.

M_fixed: Given a tripartite graph on A,B,C with |A|=|B|=n, |C|=ceil(sqrt n) and O(n^{3/2}) edges, decide for every edge whether it lies in a triangle. Bitsets give O(n^2/log n). Is there eps>0 and an O(n^{2-eps})-time (randomized allowed) algorithm? Or: show this case is as hard as balanced All-Edges Sparse Triangle (m^{4/3-o(1)}), noting m^{4/3}=n^2 here.
notes: Posed by AVW (2610.06783, Sec. 1.1 and Sec. 6, motivated by girth approximation). AVW method needs middle part <= n^{0.1204}; Majdoddin 2610.17420 extends thin products to D<=N^{0.172}, still far below 1/2. No newer preprint found. Ties directly to AVW's question whether lopsided can be easier than balanced. Original M was not a statement.

M_fixed: Assuming only (deterministic) ETH, prove there is no f(k)*n^{O(1)} algorithm that approximates (uncolored) Densest k-Subgraph within any factor g(k)=omega(1) (Gap-ETH gives k^{o(1)}, Chalermsook et al. FOCS 2017).
notes: k-Biclique disjunct already known: Lin (JACM 2018, arXiv:1406.3700) rules out f(k)n^{o(sqrt k)} under ETH (via a probabilistic construction). Constant-factor colored DkS = 2CSP already follows from PIH under ETH (GLRSW). Claim that Aggarwal et al. 2504.02695 lists DkS/k-Biclique as Gap-ETH-only is not in their abstract (a lattice paper); unverified. Remaining part is one item of a broad program.

M_fixed: For some fixed r>=3, give a single randomized algorithm that, given 1^n, samples in expected poly(n) time from a permutation-invariant distribution P_n on n-vertex graphs whose low-degree advantage over G(n,1/2) vanishes up to degree D_n=Theta((log n)^{r-1}), while after independent edge resampling at a fixed rate delta>0 a poly-time test distinguishes it from G(n,1/2) w.p. 1-o(1). Equivalently for Mao's construction: find in poly(n) time evaluation points with every <=L of the vectors phi(x_i) linearly independent.
notes: Posed by Mao (arXiv:2607.20318v2, Sec. 4): sampler needs O(n log n+(log n)^{2r}) advice; subspace made explicit via trace functions, but poly-time seed for points 'remains open'; brute force exp(O((log n)^r)). Drop the 'prove every samplable distribution is hard' disjunct: unprovable without major separations. No newer solution found.

M_fixed: Say (lambda_q)_{q<=Q} is triply well-factorable of level Q if for all Q1Q2Q3=Q there are 1-bounded alpha,beta,gamma supported on q_i<=Q_i with lambda=alpha*beta*gamma (Dirichlet convolution). Let theta* = sup of theta such that for all eps,A>0, fixed a!=0, and every such lambda of level Q=x^{theta-eps}: sum_{q<=Q,(q,a)=1} lambda_q(pi(x;q,a)-pi(x)/phi(q)) <<_{eps,A,a} x(log x)^{-A}. Known theta*>=5/8 (Pascadi). Prove theta*>5/8.
notes: Verified: Pascadi 2505.00653 Thm 1.3 gives x^{5/8-eps} unconditionally, removing Selberg dependence from Lichtman's 5/8 (unconditional 66/107). Pascadi says no more flexible setting beats 5/8 with current methods, citing quadruply well-factorable weights (heuristic remark, not a barrier theorem). No newer preprint passes 5/8 (Li 2602.20917, 2608.13299 checked). Fixed M to Pascadi's Def 1.1.

M_fixed: Let f_k(x,y)=(x+y+k sin(2 pi x), y+k sin(2 pi x)) on T^2=R^2/Z^2 (Slijepcevic's normalization; Chirikov's K equals 2 pi k), and h_m(f_k) the metric entropy w.r.t. area. Known: log(2 pi k+4)-2^{430} <= h_m(f_k) <= log(2 pi k+4) for k>=exp(2^{50000}) (Slijepcevic 2026). Prove h_m(f_k)>0 for all k>=10^6, or for at least one explicit k<=100.
notes: Verified 2611.09361 (Nov 9 2026): bound and threshold exactly as cited; abstract credits a recent OpenAI preprint for non-effective large-k positivity. Original M used sin x without saying which torus while quoting Slijepcevic's 2 pi-normalized bound, a factor-2 pi mismatch in k; fixed. Ref 2507.11375 is a Kolmogorov-typicality paper, not the OpenAI preprint.
